turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so you have about twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody from this school called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Mrs. Kalinowski is fine, and the jab is noted. I asked you who decided on the zero, Hale.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
I'm writing those times down. Times with no date, from a file I haven't seen, are not evidence. And none of it explains why that zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
Don't be cute with me. Which file, what date, and was Owen heard before you entered that zero?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, and a bad citation is a careless mistake, not proof of anything. Show me the page in the essay where he wrote it.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.

Changing your mind between an outline and a final essay is what an outline is for, Hale. You've told me about two things now and shown me neither of them, so put the outline and the essay side by side where I can read them.
And the school checker says 94%.

There it is. I have Turnitin's own guide in my bag, and it says that number should not be the sole basis for punishing a student, so either show me the documents you just described or admit that the zero rests on software.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Save it. I want to see the outline, the essay and that file with its dates, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
Nobody else is in this room, Hale, and nobody is stepping out of anything. The outline, the essay, and the dates.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
You want me to tell you how to run your own meeting? Withdraw the zero, or show me what you have.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? Ten minutes, and I still haven't seen a single page about Owen's essay.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
You had described a quotation, an October 15 outline and some times on a file, and you still haven't put any of it in front of me. Turn the screen, or I'm taking this to the principal.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.

Nothing on his record, in writing, I'll hold you to. But a rewrite for what, on what evidence you still haven't shown me, and does its mark replace the zero or sit beside it? I won't have Owen take a rewrite that admits something nobody has proved.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Pressure isn't evidence, and your own procedure doesn't expire overnight because you'd like a quick yes. Put the documents in front of me now, and put the offer in an email tonight, cc the principal.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
I don't prove anything, Hale, you do, and so far you've proved that you entered a zero before anyone called me. Helping him is getting that zero off his mark before December 1.
